rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.node_content` has three obligations: `Domain::node_content` returns a `NodeContents` value for a node; the loading and preparation needed to fingerprint and format it happen inside the read; and failures return the domain's error. The fingerprint and format clauses have their own sub-requirements, `.fingerprint` and `.format`, which are assessed separately.

- **Returns a value that can be fingerprinted and formatted.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[identities_remain_stable_and_fingerprinting_uses_the_supplied_snapshot]` reads a node through `read_snapshot`. It asserts that `snapshot.content.format()` is "before" and that `content.fingerprint()` equals the snapshot's fingerprint. It then mutates the underlying store and shows the returned value is unchanged, so the loading was complete at read time. `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requirement_edges_and_input_freshness_use_the_sdk]` does the same for the real `HabeasDomain`. It asserts `node_content(...).fingerprint()` equals the retained fingerprint, and that a changed source file gives a different fingerprint on a fresh read.
- **Preparation is part of the read.** The `Memory` test domain's `node_content` (`impl[Memory/Domain]/fn[node_content]`) returns `Err("render")` when `fail_prepare` is set. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[queued_reads_selection_and_rendering_fail_before_agent_invocation]` sets that flag and asserts `ValidationError::Graph("render")` with no dependencies recorded and no agent call. This exercises a preparation failure surfacing as the domain's error from the read.
- **Load failures return the domain's error.** The same test sets `fail_read` and asserts `Graph("read")`. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[wildcard_versions_still_check_inputs_and_errors]` asserts that `is_current` propagates `Err("read")` from `node_content`.

The tests cover the success path, the load-failure path, the preparation-failure path, and the snapshot behaviour of the returned value. All of them carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.
